items.title: How Attention Shapes Emotion: A Comparative Study of Attention Mechanisms for Speech Emotion Recognition
items.authors: Marc Casals-Salvador(Barcelona Supercomputing Center; Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya); Federico Costa(Barcelona Supercomputing Center; Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya); Rodolfo Zevallos(Barcelona Supercomputing Center); Javier Hernando(Barcelona Supercomputing Center; Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya)
items.abstract: Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) plays a key role in advancing human-computer interaction. Attention mechanisms have become the dominant approach for modeling emotional speech due to their ability to capture long-range dependencies and emphasize salient information. However, standard self-attention suffers from quadratic computational and memory complexity, limiting its scalability. In this work, we present a systematic benchmark of optimized attention mechanisms for SER, including RetNet, LightNet, GSA, FoX, and KDA. Experiments on both MSP-Podcast benchmark versions show that while standard self-attention achieves the strongest recognition performance across test sets, efficient attention variants dramatically improve scalability, reducing inference latency and memory usage by up to an order of magnitude. These results highlight a critical trade-off between accuracy and efficiency, providing practical insights for designing scalable SER systems.

items.title: From Single to Multi-Label SER: Dataset and Mamba-Based Fusion Model
items.authors: Vu Long Tran(Hanoi University of Science and Technology); Long Duc Do(Hanoi University of Science and Technology); Vinh Quang Nguyen(Hanoi University of Science and Technology); Ngoc Minh Nguyen(Hanoi University of Science and Technology); Quang Minh Le Pham(Hanoi University of Science and Technology); Hieu Trung Nguyen(Hanoi University of Science and Technology); Trang Thu Thi Nguyen(Hanoi University of Science and Technology)
items.abstract: We present a reproducible multi-label benchmark for speech emotion recognition (SER) built from the MSP-Podcast V2.0 corpus. Our pipeline converts crowdsourced emotion votes into multi-hot labels with controlled ambiguity and sparsity via reliability filtering, deterministic vote-to-label construction, and lightweight time-shift augmentation. On this benchmark, we provide a compact Mamba-based fusion baseline over MFCC and log-mel features, following prior SER fusion practice, while using linear-time state-space backbones for efficient modeling of long audio. Using a validation-only global threshold sweep for checkpoint selection and a fixed test-time threshold for evaluation, our fusion model attains competitive micro-F1 on two MSP-Podcast test partitions (≈0.50 on both Test1 and Test2) while remaining substantially lighter than heavier baselines and recent methods. We release dataset splits, construction code, and training recipes to support future work on scalable multi-label SER.

items.title: Multi-Loss Learning for Speech Emotion Recognition with Energy-Adaptive Mixup and Frame-Level Attention
items.authors: Cong Wang(Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications); Yizhong Geng(Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications); Yuhua Wen(Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications); Qifei Li(Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications); Yingming Gao(Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications); Ruimin Wang(Li Auto); Chunfeng Wang(Li Auto); Hao Li(Li Auto); Wei Chen(Li Auto); Ya Li(Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications)
items.abstract: Speech emotion recognition (SER) is an important technology in human-computer interaction. However, achieving high performance is challenging due to emotional complexity and scarce annotated data. To tackle these challenges, we propose a multi-loss learning (MLL) framework integrating an energy-adaptive mixup (EAM) method and a frame-level attention module (FLAM). The EAM method leverages SNR-based augmentation to generate diverse speech samples capturing subtle emotional variations. FLAM enhances frame-level feature extraction for multi-frame emotional cues. Our MLL strategy combines Kullback-Leibler divergence, focal, center, and supervised contrastive loss to optimize learning, address class imbalance, and improve feature separability. We evaluate our method on four widely used SER datasets: IEMOCAP, MSP-IMPROV, RAVDESS, and SAVEE. The results demonstrate our method achieves state-of-the-art performance, suggesting its effectiveness and robustness.

items.title: Segment-wise Embedding based Graph Attention Network for Effective Speech Emotion Recognition
items.authors: Haoyu Song(Singapore Institute of Technology); Ian McLoughlin(Singapore Institute of Technology); Yan Song(University of Science and Technology of China); Lirong Dai(University of Science and Technology of China)
items.abstract: With the advancement of pretrained speech models like Hubert-large, leveraging general representations for downstream tasks such as speech emotion recognition (SER) is of growing importance to both academia and industry. We propose a highly effective segment-wise embedding-domain graph-attention network (GAT) where a Swin-Transformer adapts a pretrained model to capture multi-scale information from utterances. Self-supervised adaptor post-training with both block masking prediction and utterance-level contrastive learning addresses distribution shift issues. During finetuning, a graph is constructed from multiple embedding crops per utterance, allowing GAT-based temporal aggregation to extract insightful information from variable-length utterances. In addition to cross entropy, supervised contrastive learning is used to improve robustness to ambiguous utterance labels. Extensive SER experiments on IEMOCAP and MER2023 demonstrate significant performance gains over SOTA solutions.

items.title: Dual-Stream DNN-KAN Networks with Bangla-Specific Features for Speech Emotion Recognition
items.authors: Kazi Reyazul Hasan(Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology); Muhammad Abdullah Adnan(Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology)
items.abstract: Speech emotion recognition (SER) is challenging due to the complex interplay of spectral and prosodic features. We propose a dual-stream DNN-KAN architecture for Bangla speech, processing MFCCs through efficient DNN blocks and statistically optimized prosodic features via lightweight Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) with learnable B-spline activations. With only 1.1M parameters, our model achieves 92.12% on SUBESCO and 82.79% on BanglaSER under speaker-independent (SI) evaluation. Most prior Bangla SER work omits SI evaluation, so published figures likely reflect speaker memorization rather than genuine generalization. Re-running our feature-selection pipeline on EmoDB yields 93.92%, showing that the selection methodology transfers across languages. At 1.1M parameters, the model surpasses emotion2vec (25M) by 2.70% and wav2vec2-xlsr (326M) by 1.07% on SUBESCO SI, showing that statistically grounded feature engineering can match large pre-trained models at a fraction of the cost.

items.title: EII-SCL: Harnessing Emotional Inertia for Multimodal Emotion Recognition in Conversation
items.authors: Zilong Huang(The Hong Kong Polytechnic University); Kong Aik Lee(The Hong Kong Polytechnic University); Chong-xin Gan(The Hong Kong Polytechnic University); Zezhong Jin(The Hong Kong Polytechnic University); Ruichen Zuo(The Hong Kong Polytechnic University); Man-Wai Mak(The Hong Kong Polytechnic University)
items.abstract: Multimodal emotion recognition in conversation (MERC) achieves accurate predictions by integrating multimodal and contextual information in dialogues. While current MERC approaches focus on modeling complex contextual dependencies in conversation, they often overlook the impact of contextual emotional inertia in emotion shift, leading to suboptimal performance. To address this issue, we propose a novel Emotional Inertia-Informed Supervised Contrastive Learning module (EII-SCL) that informs the contrastive objective by constructing inertia-affected samples within temporal windows, effectively leveraging emotional inertia as a prior while enabling seamless integration with existing MERC models without requiring additional data. Extensive experiments on IEMOCAP and MELD show that our approach consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods.

items.title: Leveraging Modality-Specific Label Distributions for Enhanced Multimodal Emotion Recognition
items.authors: Xiaohan Shi(Nagoya University); Xingfeng Li(City University of Macau); Tomoki Toda(Nagoya University)
items.abstract: Multimodal emotion recognition (MER) aims to recognize human emotions by jointly modeling multiple modalities. Existing approaches mainly focus on learning modality-specific representations through complex fusion strategies, often overlooking the potential value of modality-specific label distributions. To address this limitation, we propose MoLD, a Modality-specific Label Distribution-based framework that explicitly models modality-specific label distributions to enhance MER. Meanwhile, we introduce a modality similarity loss to enforce cross-modal consistency. In this study, we compare MoLD with representative baselines and conduct ablation studies to analyze the contribution of each component. Additionally, we evaluate the model under unimodal settings to assess its robustness. Experimental results demonstrate that MoLD consistently outperforms benchmark baselines, with each component contributing to overall performance and maintaining effectiveness under unimodal settings.

items.title: Learning from Annotation Uncertainty: Entropy-Aware Curriculum for Speech Emotion Recognition
items.authors: Zahra Omidi(University of Texas at Dallas); John Hansen(University of Texas at Dallas)
items.abstract: Speech emotion recognition (SER) often relies on hard consensus labels that collapse annotator disagreement. We study distribution-based supervision for 9-class SER on MSP-Podcast 2.0 using a WavLM-Base multitask model for categorical emotion and dimensional VAD. Hard-label training is compared with targets from primary and merged primary–secondary annotator vote distributions. Distributional objectives improve alignment with human vote distributions, reducing JSD/KLD relative to hard-label training. Analysis shows that hard supervision partly benefits from assigning ambiguous utterances to the residual Other class, whereas distributional supervision redistributes uncertainty across emotion categories. Entropy-stratified evaluation shows that high-ambiguity utterances remain challenging, but distribution-based supervision better captures perceptual uncertainty. These findings support moving beyond hard labels toward targets that reflect listener disagreement.

items.title: Revisiting Delay Compensation via Feature-Level Temporal Accumulation in Continuous Emotion Recognition
items.authors: Jian Xiang(The University of New South Wales); Jingyao Wu(Massachesetts Institute of Technology); Ting Dang(The University of Melbourne); Vidhyasaharan Sethu(The University of New South Wales); Eliathamby Ambikairajah(The University of New South Wales)
items.abstract: Continuous emotion recognition (CER) relies on time-continuous annotations that reflect annotators' sustained emotion perception. In practice, ground-truth annotations are often observed to have a lag, which leads to temporal misalignment between model predictions and annotator labels. The most common solution is delay compensation based on a relative temporal shift between input and labels, assuming that annotations are delayed reports of judgements formed based on the signal at a given moment. While effective, this shift-based delay compensation (SDC) requires explicit temporal shifting and truncation at sequence boundaries, and its performance can be sensitive to the choice of delay parameter. In this paper, we revisit delay compensation and introduce accumulated delay compensation (ADC), implemented via feature-level temporal accumulation. Instead of explicitly shifting labels, ADC accumulates past input features, incorporating historical context while inducing an intrinsic delay without modifying the original input–label alignment. Experiments on the RECOLA corpus demonstrate ADC is substantially more robust to the choice of delay parameter when compared with SDC. Further analysis reveals dimension-specific temporal effects: arousal favours shorter integration windows, whereas valence benefits from a longer window. These findings suggest that ADC offers a superior approach for delay compensation compared to the standard approach for CER.

items.title: Two-Sided Fairness Transfer for Gender-Neutral Speech Emotion Recognition with Partially Observed Attributes
items.authors: Woan-Shiuan Chien(National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University); Tomohiko Nakamura(AIST); Huan-Yu Chen(National Tsing Hua University); Satoru Fukayama(AIST); Hitoshi Suda(AIST); Jun Ogata(AIST); Chi-Chun Lee(National Tsing Hua University)
items.abstract: Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) powers applications by interpreting users' emotions from speech. Ensuring fairness in SER is inherently a two-sided challenge, as a truly fair system requires neutrality to both speaker-side and rater-side biases. However, existing debiasing methods rely on explicit attribute labels for both sides, which are often unavailable. In this work, we address the challenge of cross-dataset fairness transfer under partial attribute supervision, where only one side (speaker or rater) has gender labels in the target dataset. We present a two-stage framework that first fine-tunes a pre-trained CLAP model with an adversarial debiasing objective to build one-sided gender-neutral models. We then introduce the ATT2Fair task vector, derived from the difference between speaker- and rater-side fair models in a source dataset, and apply it to infer the absent-side fair model in the target dataset. Our results highlight the practicality of fairness transfer for building gender-neutral SER systems across diverse datasets.

items.title: Conflict-Aware Pseudo-Labeling via Acoustic Signals for Multi-Task Speech Emotion Recognition
items.authors: Haojie Zhou(Jiangnan University; Engineering Research Center of Intelligent Technology for Healthcare, Ministry of Education, Jiangnan University); Shunfei Liang(Jiangnan University); Chengze Li(Jiangnan University); Zhizhong Bai(Jiangnan University); Yicheng Feng(Jiangnan University); Ning Wang(Jiangnan University; Engineering Research Center of Intelligent Technology for Healthcare, Ministry of Education, Jiangnan University)
items.abstract: Speech Emotion Recognition (SER) typically relies on utterance-level annotations, obscuring temporal emotional dynamics. While recent multi-task approaches achieve fine-grained alignment via Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), they heavily depend on costly human transcripts. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel Conflict-Aware Pseudo-Labeling method that derives frame-level auxiliary supervision solely from acoustic signals. Using collaborative inference across diverse data partitions, it adaptively segments speech into consensus and conflict regions. We assign hard pseudo-labels to consensus frames to capture local discriminative cues, while introducing a global back-filling mechanism to rectify conflict regions using the utterance-level label as a global prior, mitigating pseudo-label noise. Experiments on three datasets, IEMOCAP, EmoDB, and MELD, show that our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance without auxiliary text or elaborate structural redesigns.
